question: Why are the many rival schools said to fall short of knowing Shiva-tattva?
premises: The scripture challenges as many as three hundred and sixty-three disputants.
Those disputants discriminate only within a limited range.
Limited discrimination cannot grasp the full higher principle.
inference: The rival schools are rejected because their knowledge extends only to a partial domain.
uncertainties: The number three hundred and sixty-three is taken as a traditional count of rival views.
plain_english: Thus, as many as three hundred and sixty-three disputants are challenged, for they discriminate only within that limited measure.
